messages:
jon.k: heads-up — after the v3.12 canary rollout I'm seeing heatmaps and sparklines hang on first paint in prod-eu. long tasks ~200-600ms, CPU parse spikes. reproducible on a few accounts. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deployed console/v3.12 canary -> eu (weight 10%) at 2026-03-20T09:17:03Z

sam: ugh. any correlation with the prefetch/kv change from yesterday?

maya: possible — we flipped routing-affinity TTL from 30s -> 5s for better rebalancing. that could cause more kvcache churn.

rafa: telemetry shows kvcache miss rate jumped from 8% -> 52% for tile fetches right after the canary window started. metric tiles in particular.

jon.k: repro steps: 1) load dashboard with 6+ heatmap tiles, 2) observe long tasks and delayed chart paints, 3) repeat a few times. attaching stack-ish logs below:
```
[perf] kvcache: miss key=tile:v2:heatmap:abcd TTL=4s route=eu-a
[perf] parse main.chunk.js 420ms
[perf] render heatmap 320ms
```

liz: interesting — we also shipped a tiny embedlib update that inlines a locale bundle into the main chunk (to avoid a 2nd chunk roundtrip). that may explain parse bloat.

sam: so two axes: (1) kvcache thrash -> rehydrate + fetches -> CPU, (2) main chunk bloat -> parse time. either could push long tasks over the LCP threshold.

maya: agree. quick mitigation options: rollback embedlib inline OR restore affinity TTL to 30s OR reduce canary weight. which do we prefer for fastest turnaround?

rafa: telemetry-wise, reducing canary weight to 0 is fastest and gives us time to investigate. but if main chunk parse is the bigger contributor, rollback of embedlib change would be best. can we get rough numbers?

jon.k: i sketched a quick experiment: disable client-side prefetching via feature flag for canary only, see if miss rate drops and CPU spikes reduce. that should be reversible w/o full rollback.

liz: feature flag is ready: `client.prefetch.enabled` can be toggled per-route. we can flip for eu-canary in <5m.

deploy-bot: toggled client.prefetch.enabled = false for console-eu-canary at 2026-03-20T09:29:10Z

sam: after flag flip we still see some parse spikes but heatmap hangs reduced in my quick smoke. need 10-20 minutes to gather stable telemetry.

rafa: confirmed in metrics: kvcache miss rate dropped from 52% -> 12% for canary bucket after flag flip. long task count down ~60%.

liz: that points to kvcache churn being the primary culprit. chunk parse still matters but less catastrophic.

maya: plan proposal: 1) keep prefetch disabled on canary + pause rollout, 2) revert routing-affinity TTL change in canary env only (restore 30s), 3) run perf harness and telemetry for 1 hour, 4) iterate on embedlib inline separately (size-critical).

sam: i'm +1. we should also add a telemetry tag to all chart loads (prefetch=true/false, affinity-ttl=X) so we can A/B quickly next time.

jon.k: added a tracking ticket in #eng-platform-board: https://redwood.internal/issue/INFR-4321 (perf harness + telemetry tags).

liz: quick follow-up — embedlib inline increased main.chunk gzip size by ~18KB. not huge but combined with churn it nudges parse. maybe we can ship a smaller locale subset instead of full inline. i'll prototype.

rafa: re: routing policy, we should add an emergency circuit: if kvcache miss rate > 20% for 5m, revert affinity to previous TTL automatically. could be a simple runbook -> automation.

maya: agree, I'll file a short RFC for affinity safety-guard and add to rollout checklist.

sam: final ask: let's not do global TTL flips without perf canaries next time :grimacing:. small changes can cascade.

jon.k: agreed. thanks all — keeping canary paused and prefetch off. will report back after 1h telemetry window. :thumbsup:
